Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Summary of current findings: Acute dry, itchy rash on arms and hands, onset a few days ago; localized to exposed areas; no fever or systemic symptoms; redness noted; symptoms began after swimming; coconut butter used without relief; reports fatigue but overall well; no known prior skin disease
- Supporting differential diagnoses (aligned with transcript and DDx):
  - Irritant contact dermatitis — High likelihood
  - Allergic contact dermatitis — Moderate likelihood
  - Atopic dermatitis (eczema) — Moderate likelihood
  - Xerosis/dry skin — Low likelihood as primary diagnosis
- Conflicts: Not recorded

Management Plan
- Treatment/interventions:
  - Topical corticosteroid cream for inflammation
  - Emollients for dry skin
  - Over-the-counter antihistamines for itch (e.g., Piriton or Loratadine)
  - Paracetamol not indicated for this presentation
  - Return visit in 1 week if not improved or symptoms worsen
- Education/advise:
  - Avoid potential triggers such as pool-related irritants and newly applied products (e.g., coconut butter)
  - Continue skin care with emollients and monitor response
  - Consider escalation if symptoms persist or spread
- Follow-up: If not improving after a week, re-evaluate

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Irritant contact dermatitis — High
  - Justification: Acute onset after swimming; exposed areas (hands/arms); dry, red, itchy skin; no systemic symptoms
- Allergic contact dermatitis — Moderate
  - Justification: Possible exposure to pool chemicals, soaps, or coconut butter; pruritus and localized erythema
- Atopic dermatitis — Moderate
  - Justification: Family history of atopy (asthma, hayfever); dry, itchy skin; hands/arms prone to involvement
- Xerosis/dry skin — Low
  - Justification: Prominent dryness; weather factors may contribute; less inflammatory than dermatitis
